page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-75s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU, and the instance includes 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU package provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2 instructions. No hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside limited parallel throughput due to the small core count. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server achieved 2,929.97, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems, matched with an average Geekbench single-core score of 1817.0. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (5,812.19) and Geekbench multi-core (3,297.0) rank in the bottom 25%. Decompression and compression benchmarks show consistent middle-tier speeds, including single-threaded gzip compression at 27.69 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 11.33 GB/sec.

Subsystems with heavy concurrency or memory bandwidth demands exhibit performance constraints. The PassMark database operations metric fell into the bottom 10% at 935.72, and static web serving throughput reached 2.39 GB/sec. Large block read memory bandwidth registered at 38.07 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measured 34.24 GB/sec. Redis SET operations yielded 3.82 million operations per second, reflecting limits imposed by the two-vCPU topology.

Qualitatively, the server provides cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for small services that require consistent CPU access without burst throttling. The pairing of dedicated AMD EPYC compute and local NVMe storage provides predictable behavior for modest operational demands. Suitable workloads include lightweight API gateways, single-threaded batch processing, utility microservices, development environments, and small-scale automation workers.
description: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-75s-amd is an entry-tier instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core with 2 threads) on an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware profile includes 4.0 GB of RAM, a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded CPU capability, scoring in the top 25% on single-core stress-ng tests. However, the limited core count places its multi-core, database, and high-concurrency throughput metrics in lower percentiles, such as 2.39 GB/sec in static web serving. This configuration provides a stable, dedicated compute environment suited for non-bursting, single-threaded utilities, microservices, lightweight background processing, and low-scale application hosting.
